Mutation fixture (lane mrental), predicted by hand from the archived sources before running the evaluator. royalty.yaml note and i1040se p. 6: r is a royalty from the filer's own business (Schedule C), s claims depletion (line 18); both are outside this tool and each line 21 is refused at its own condition.

royalty[r].line21.form: Schedule C (royalties from your own trade or business)
royalty[r].line21.remedy: Royalties from your own business or services (as a self-employed writer, artist, inventor or other creator, or name, image and likeness income from sponsorships or services), or from a working interest, are reported on Schedule C; this tool does not prepare them on Schedule E.

cite.locator: p. 6, Line 4, "If you are in business as a self-employed writer, inventor, artist, etc., report your royalty income and expenses on Schedule C"

cases.evidence_note: Lane MF, predicted by hand from the archived sources before running the evaluator. Royalties of $5,000 with a payment for a patent the filer transferred (i1040se p. 6: such amounts may be treated as the sale of a capital asset); outside this tool, so Schedule E line 21 for the royalty refuses at that question.

royalty[r].line21.form: Form 4797 or Schedule D (patent transfer, or coal or iron ore)
royalty[r].line21.remedy: Royalties that may be treated as the sale of a capital asset (from a patent you transferred, or coal or iron ore you disposed of) are outside this tool.

cite.locator: p. 6, "You may be able to treat amounts received as 'royalties' for the transfer of a patent or amounts received on the disposal of coal and iron ore as the sale of a capital asset"

royalty[r].line21.remedy: Car, truck and travel costs of a royalty are outside this tool.

cases.evidence_note: Lane MF, predicted by hand from the archived sources before running the evaluator. Royalties $200 and legal fees $500: line 21 -300, a loss; part of the investment was borrowed without personal liability. i1040se p. 3, At-Risk Rules, and p. 7, Line 21: Form 6198 figures the deductible loss, which this tool does not, so the royalty loss and Schedule E line 26 refuse at the at-risk question.

sche.line26.remedy: A royalty with an amount not at risk is outside this tool, in a year with a loss and in a year with income (when the amount at risk falls below zero, losses deducted earlier are recaptured).

cite.locator: p. 3, At-Risk Rules; p925 p. 19, At-Risk Limits, "If your losses from an at-risk activity are allowed, they’re subject to recapture in later years if your amount at risk is reduced below zero"

cases.evidence_note: Lane rentals (2026-11-24), predicted by hand before running the evaluator: royalties of $5,000 whose earlier return had Form 6198 (p925 p. 19: an at-risk carryover or recapture); every other royalty screen answer is No by default, so Schedule E line 21 for the royalty refuses at that question.

royalty[r].line21.remedy: A royalty with Form 6198 on an earlier return, or a loss held back because amounts were not at risk, can carry that loss into 2025 or owe recapture of losses allowed before; this tool does not prepare Form 6198.

cite.locator: p. 19, At-Risk Limits, "You treat any loss that is disallowed because of the at-risk limits as a deduction from the same activity in the next tax year"
